actions.text: Received in the Senate. Read twice. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 64.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 415 - 9 (Roll no. 109). (text: 04/28/2025 CR H1666-1667)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 415 - 9 (Roll no. 109). (text: 04/28/2025 CR H1666-1667)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H1710-1711)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 859.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H1666)
Mr. Bilirakis moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 49.
Reported by the Committee on Energy and Commerce. H. Rept. 119-72.
Reported by the Committee on Energy and Commerce. H. Rept. 119-72.
Ordered to be Reported by Voice Vote.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

dimensions.assessment: Affects manufacturers of smart consumer devices and consumers purchasing internet-connected products.
dimensions.evidence: Each manufacturer of a covered device shall disclose, clearly and conspicuously and prior to purchase

dimensions.assessment: Requires labeling and pre-purchase disclosures for covered smart devices without banning products or altering core technologies.
dimensions.evidence: disclose, clearly and conspicuously and prior to purchase, whether the covered device manufactured by the manufacturer contains a camera or microphone

dimensions.assessment: Does not specify federal spending levels or direct appropriations, relying on existing FTC enforcement mechanisms.
Establishes a new federal disclosure mandate enforced through the Federal Trade Commission Act.
dimensions.evidence: A violation of section 2 shall be treated as a violation of a rule defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent labeling and disclosure requirement for future manufactured consumer electronics.
dimensions.evidence: This Act shall apply to all covered devices manufactured after the date that is 180 days after the date on which guidance is issued

missing_information: Specific economic compliance costs for manufacturers to alter product packaging or listings.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires manufacturers of certain internet-connected devices with cameras or microphones to provide pre-purchase disclosures, enforced by the FTC as an unfair or deceptive practice.
